harmonicFunction: Dm (i) - Heavy, dark minor tonic driving the narrative forward
C (♭VII) - Subtonic chord maintaining natural minor propulsion
G/B (IV6) - Inverted Dorian-leaning major IV chord with the B natural bass note providing uplifting contrast
Bb (♭VI) - Dark submediant chord locking into the natural minor resolution
A (V) - Major dominant in the chorus providing definitive harmonic tension and resolution back to Dm

techniques.name: Expressive Vox Wah-Wah Articulation & Descending Chords
techniques.description: Rhythmically sweeping a wah-wah pedal in tandem with picking dynamics to turn guitar lead lines into crying vocal statements

notes: Descending bassline: D (open D string) → C (3rd fret A) → B (2nd fret A) → Bb (1st fret A) → C (3rd fret A)
Solo in 10th-position D minor pentatonic on strings 1, 2, and 3
Sweeping wah pedal from heel (bass) to toe (treble) on sustained bends
sequence: Fret the Dm chord and transition cleanly down the A-string bass walk
Accent beat 1 of each chord change with authority
Engage wah pedal with toe forward on the attack, rocking back on the sustain
Lock into Ginger Baker's driving four-on-the-floor drum groove
tips: Don't sweep the wah pedal mechanically—match the sweep to the emotional contour of your phrases
Clapton used 'The Fool' 1964 Gibson SG into a cranked Marshall 100W Super Lead for thick sustain
Emphasize the B natural bass note in the G/B chord for authentic voice leading

techniques.name: Stepwise Bass Voice-Leading & 5/4 Metric Articulation
techniques.description: Fretting smooth stepwise bass transitions across inverted chords while locking with odd-meter drum and timpani accents

notes: Count the 5/4 intro precisely: ONE-two-three-FOUR-five
G/B inverted chord: fret 2 on A string (B bass), open D and G strings, fret 3 on B string (D)
Bb barre: fret 1 on A string, frets 3 on D, G, and B strings
sequence: Strike the low G power chord on beat 1 of the 5/4 fanfare
Let timpani roll carry the measure into the resolving Dm crash
Execute the verse bassline without stopping the ringing treble strings
Drive into the major A dominant chord at the end of the chorus
tips: Keep the index finger relaxed when moving from G/B to Bb
Use a firm downstroke on the bass string before strumming the remainder of each chord
Listen to Jack Bruce's bass guitar to ensure octave alignment on the descending walkdown

sections.name: 5/4 Meter Fanfare
sections.description: The ominous 5/4 intro cadence featuring heavy crash cymbals and stately descending chords.
notes: Count carefully: 1-2-3-4-5 per measure
Let the low Dm chord rumble with tube sustain
Prepare for the tempo surge into the 4/4 verse

sections.name: Descending Verse Progression (Dm to Bb)
sections.technique: Expressive Vox Wah-Wah Articulation & Descending Chords
sections.description: The driving 4/4 verse chord progression moving Dm to C, G/B, and Bb.
notes: Highlight the descending bassline on the A string
Drive with solid eighth-note pick attack
Smooth transition between G/B and Bb

sections.name: Chorus Power Cadence (C - G - Bb - A)
sections.description: Triumphant rock cadence resolving on the powerful major dominant A chord.
notes: Hit the C and G chords with heavy arena downstrokes
Let the major A chord ring to create harmonic resolution tension
Tight snare synchronicity on beats 2 and 4

sections.name: Wah-Wah Solo Statement (Chorus 1)
sections.technique: Expressive Vox Wah-Wah Articulation & Descending Chords
sections.description: Clapton's opening wah-wah lead statement wailing over the verse progression.
notes: Rock the wah pedal forward on peak bends
Use full-step bends on the 13th fret B string to high D
Sustain notes with wide, singing vibrato

sections.name: Wah-Wah Solo Climax & Upper Register (Chorus 2)
sections.technique: Expressive Vox Wah-Wah Articulation & Descending Chords
sections.description: Rapid 10th-position pentatonic flourishes and screaming bent notes with full wah pedal sweep.
notes: High-velocity sixteenth-note pull-offs between frets 13 and 10
Full wah sweep emphasizing cutting treble frequencies
Wide vibrato on the 13th fret high E string

sections.name: Outro Wah Jam & Polyrhythmic Coda
sections.technique: Expressive Vox Wah-Wah Articulation & Descending Chords
sections.description: Relentless continuous wah-wah improvisation locking with Ginger Baker's four-on-the-floor beat into the fade.
notes: Maintain continuous rhythmic foot sweep on the wah pedal
Trade melodic phrases against Baker's polyrhythmic drumming
Decay into final tape fade

guitar.pickup: Bridge humbucker for cutting wah lead; neck humbucker with tone rolled off for 'woman tone'

amp.recommended: Marshall 100W Super Lead Plexi (1968 spec) & 4x12 Basketweave cab

effects.distortion: Cranked Marshall 100W Super Lead Plexi power tube saturation
effects.wah: Vox Clyde McCoy Wah-Wah (essential for authentic vocal sweep)

beginner.title: Verse Chord Progression
steps: Learn the five verse chords: Dm, C, G/B, Bb, and C
Practice the descending bassline on the A string at 80 BPM
Strum in steady quarter notes without stopping

intermediate.title: 5/4 Intro & Chorus
steps: Count and perform the 5/4 intro cadence with correct timing
Master the high-energy chorus progression (C - G - Bb - A)
Play along with the studio track at 110 BPM

advanced.title: Wah-Wah Solo Mastery
steps: Coordinate foot movement on the wah pedal with right-hand pick attacks
Master Clapton's 10th-position D minor pentatonic solo vocabulary
Improvise over the looping verse progression with authentic 1968 psychedelic tone

commonMistakes: Losing the count in the 5/4 meter intro
Sweeping the wah pedal out of sync with your musical phrases
Muting the B-natural bass note in the G/B chord
practiceRoutine: 5 minutes: 5/4 intro counting and chord timing
5 minutes: Descending verse walkdown at 90 BPM → 110 BPM
5 minutes: Wah pedal sweep coordination drill on single notes
metronomeWork: Set metronome to 5/4 at 90 BPM for the intro
Switch to 4/4 at 110 BPM for the verse and solo sections
